content: Veratrum is an over-the-counter (OTC) medication that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of acute, self-limiting conditions based on standard homeopathic indications. It is primarily indicated for the management of diarrhea and vomiting. The recommended dosage is to take the medication at the onset of symptoms, repeating every two hours or as needed until relief is achieved. If symptoms persist or worsen, the use of the medication should be discontinued, and a healthcare practitioner should be consulted. The medication can be administered by dissolving 5-10 pellets in 1 ounce of filtered water or taken dry by mouth, with a typical dose being 1-5 pellets. There is limited information available regarding the off-label use of Veratrum in both adults and pediatric patients, whether supported by guidelines or not. Similarly, there is limited data on its FDA-labeled use in pediatric patients. Contraindications for Veratrum are not well-documented in the drug label. Pregnant or nursing individuals are advised to consult a healthcare practitioner before using this medication. Additionally, all medications, including Veratrum, should be kept out of the reach of children. Adverse reactions to Veratrum have not been extensively studied, and there is limited information regarding clinical trial experiences or post-marketing data. Similarly, there is limited information on drug interactions, monitoring requirements, IV compatibility, and overdose management for Veratrum. The pharmacological details of Veratrum, including its mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology, are not well-documented in the drug label. The active ingredient in Veratrum is Veratrum album, and the inactive ingredients include lactose and sucrose. There is no FDA guidance on the use of Veratrum in specific populations, including pregnant individuals, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Additionally, there is no specific guidance for its use in relation to gender, race, or immunocompromised patients. Veratrum is administered orally, but there is limited information on its monitoring requirements or storage conditions. The interaction between Veratrum and alcohol has not been established, and patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while taking this medication. The brand name associated with Veratrum is Diarrhea Vomiting®. There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names for Veratrum in the drug label.
